verdict.rationale: Rollbar documents a public RESTful API that its own official SDKs use to report errors, and explicitly says it can be used to create notifiers for additional languages. A post_client_item token scope exists for sending events, a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1 spec covers Item/Occurrence resources, and the docs note community-built platform support. Missing for 10: the occurrence/item ingestion payload schema is not shown in the evidence, and there is no independent hands-on corroboration of third-party custom clients.

support.subject: As a developer, the event-ingestion protocol is documented and open enough that custom clients and compatible SDKs can send events without an official SDK

citations.quote: The Rollbar API provides a RESTful interface to much of the data in the system. It is used by our official SDKs to report errors/exceptions, deploys, and other mes
It can be used to create notifiers for additional languages, get data out to integrate with other systems, or whatever else you can imagine.
The client-side access token can only be used to send events and only from client-side platforms.
Rollbar supports over a dozen platforms, and our community has built many more.
